h1: The 6 Best Clip-On Video Lights for Calls and Streaming, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Clip-On Video Lighting: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 clip-on video lights for laptops and monitors, compared on colour accuracy, adjustability and mounting, all under $25.
summary: The ALTSON 60 LED clip light is the best clip-on video light for most people, because it is the only one that discloses a CRI of 97 or higher and it runs on its own rechargeable battery. The five-colour, five-brightness kit is the best adjustable ring light, the Cyezcor is the proven simple choice, and the Evershop adds a desk stand.
intro: A clip-on light fixes the most common video-call problem, a face lit only by a glowing screen, but it creates a new one if you buy blind. A cheap ring light parked on top of a monitor often throws a harsh white circle into the lenses of anyone who wears glasses and flattens your face with light from straight ahead. The fix is not more brightness but better control and better colour.

This ranking sorts six clip-on lights, all costing under $25, by the features that decide how you look on camera: colour rendering, adjustability, power source and mounting flexibility. Each pick was judged on its specification text as written; brightness figures that a listing omits are left out here too.

products.name: ALTSON 60 LED Portable Selfie Light Video Conference Lighting with Clip & Camera Tripod Adapter, Rechargeable 2200mAh, CRI 97+
products.verdict: The only light here that discloses a CRI of 97 or higher, with a rechargeable 2200mAh battery.
products.description:
The ALTSON has 60 LEDs, a stated CRI of 97 plus, a rechargeable 2200mAh battery, three light modes, a clip and a tripod adapter. It costs under $25.

It wins because colour rendering is the quality that separates a flattering light from a harsh one. CRI measures how faithfully a light shows colours, and a figure of 97 means skin tones look natural instead of grey or green. A built-in battery means no cable dangling across your keyboard, and the tripod adapter adds a second mounting route if the clip does not suit your laptop.

Buy it for calls where you want to look natural. Skip it if you need continuous all-day use without recharging.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants natural skin tones on calls.

products.name: Video Conference Lighting Kit, Ring Light Clip on Laptop Monitor with 5 Dimmable Color & 5 Brightness Level
products.verdict: Five colour temperatures and five brightness levels on a laptop-and-monitor clip.
products.description:
This ring light clips to a laptop or monitor and offers five colour temperature settings and five brightness levels, for webcam, Zoom and streaming use. It costs under $25.

It ranks second because adjustability is the most practical feature at this price. Five colour settings let you match your room, warm for a lamp-lit evening and cool for a window-lit day, while five brightness steps stop you overpowering a small face. It does not publish a CRI, so we cannot compare colour accuracy with the leader.

Choose it if you call from rooms with changing light. Skip it if colour accuracy is your first concern.
products.idealFor: Callers in rooms with changing light.

products.name: Cyezcor Video Conference Lighting Kit, Ring Light for Monitor Clip On
products.verdict: A straightforward clip-on ring light with adjustable brightness and a long market record.
products.description:
The Cyezcor is a ring light with a clip-on monitor mount and adjustable brightness, sold as a video conference kit. It costs under $25.

It ranks third because it is the most established design in the group, which tends to mean fewer surprises with the clip and controls. The listing offers adjustable brightness but no colour temperature range or CRI, so it is a good light but a less versatile one than the two above.

Buy it for a simple, no-fuss upgrade. Skip it if you want colour adjustment.
products.idealFor: People wanting a plain, working light.

products.name: Evershop Ring Light for Laptop Desk Clip On, Small Computer Video Conference Lighting with Stand
products.verdict: A 5 inch ring light that clips to a screen or stands on a desk.
products.description:
The Evershop is a 5 inch ring light that clips on or sits on a stand, designed for phones, webcams and monitors. It costs under $25.

It ranks fourth because the stand option is useful, but the 5 inch ring is small. Clip or stand means you can put it on a monitor, a laptop, or a desk beside the camera, which helps when a screen is too thin for a clip. The small ring delivers a softer fill than a larger one.

Pick it if your screen is awkward to clip to. Skip it if you want a larger light.
cons: No CRI or colour range listed
products.skipIf: You want a larger, brighter ring.

products.name: Anautin Ring Light for Video Conference Lighting, 360 degrees Adjustable, Portable LED
products.verdict: A 360 degree adjustable clip-on light, listed as the most affordable in the group.
products.description:
The Anautin ring light clips to monitors, laptops and desktop computers and adjusts through 360 degrees. It costs under $25 and is the cheapest here.

It ranks fifth because the pivot lets you angle light off-axis, which reduces glare in glasses, and that is a real advantage. The listing offers little else, so brightness, colour range and battery details are unknown.

Buy it if you want to aim the light freely on a tight budget. Skip it if you want specifications.
products.idealFor: Bargain buyers wanting to aim the light.

products.name: InnoGear Ring Light for Computer On-Camera Monitor Video Conference Light
products.verdict: A simple, fixed on-camera clip light with no extra mounting options.
products.description:
The InnoGear is a compact ring light with a fixed on-camera monitor clip, focused on video conferencing. It costs under $25.

It ranks last because the fixed clip offers no angle adjustment or alternative mount. The simplicity can be a virtue if you want to clip it on and forget it, but the light sits exactly where the clip puts it, which can mean glare for glasses wearers.

Buy it if you want the simplest possible light. Skip it if you wear glasses or need adjustment.
products.skipIf: You wear glasses or need to aim it.

whatMatters.detail: CRI is a score out of 100 for how accurately a light shows colour. A figure of 90 or more suits video, and 97 is excellent. Most cheap lights do not publish it, so a disclosed CRI is a sign of a better product.
Warm light is yellow and cool light is blue-white. A range of settings lets you match your room so your face does not look orange or grey. Look for words like colour modes or dimmable colour.
Too much light in a small room washes you out. Several brightness steps let you set fill without glare. Check the number of levels, not just a lumen claim.
A ring light on top of a monitor lights you from straight ahead, which can flatten features and reflect in glasses. Angle the light slightly off-axis if the clip allows it.
A rechargeable battery means no cable crossing your desk, but you must recharge it. A cabled light runs as long as you like. Choose by how long your calls usually last.

faq.q: Will these clip onto any monitor?
faq.a: Most clip to screens of reasonable thickness, but very thin or curved monitors can be tricky. The Evershop's stand option is the best fallback.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with video lighting?
faq.a: Lighting from behind or straight on at full brightness. Place the light slightly above eye level and turn the brightness down until your face looks natural.

faq.q: Is the ALTSON worth it over the five-colour kit?
faq.a: If natural skin tones matter, yes, thanks to its disclosed CRI. If you move rooms and need colour temperature options, the five-colour kit is more flexible.
Easy. Clip it on, power it up and choose a brightness. Charge the ALTSON before first use.

faq.q: How do I keep them in good shape?
faq.a: Wipe the LEDs with a soft cloth, avoid bending the clip arm and recharge battery models before they run flat.

faq.q: Can I use them with my phone?
faq.a: The ALTSON and Evershop list phone use, and their stand or tripod options help. Others are aimed at monitors and laptops.

finalTake: The ALTSON 60 LED clip light is the best clip-on video light under $25, with a disclosed CRI of 97 plus and a rechargeable battery. The five-colour, five-brightness ring light is the adjustable choice, the Cyezcor is the proven simple option and the Evershop suits awkward screens. Angle the light off-axis if you wear glasses.
